answer: Because the quill ledger attributes every share, the signal audit shows the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. Only 61% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not pay. A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, and therefore it pays the thread fee twice and still divides one payout. That is 24 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
